observation.visible_scene: A wooden plank floor. The excerpt contains two distinct camera views separated by a hard editing cut. The first view (frames 1-18) shows scattered objects: a white T-shaped block with a small green piece, a flat white rectangular block, a green 'GO' sign with a red block beside it, a blue block, and a long row of white dominoes running along the upper right with a single green domino near its end. The second view (frames 19-41) shows an S-shaped / infinity-loop chain of standing red, yellow and green dominoes, with a short row of white dominoes at the lower-left end and another short white row at the upper-right end.
visible_changes: First view: a green domino piece near the right white row moves steadily toward the top-right corner of the frame across the sequence, while the white row on the right displays a left-to-right falling wave that advances along the row.
Hard cut between frame 18 and frame 19 replaces the first layout with the S-shaped colored chain; this is an edit, not continuous motion.
Second view: the left white domino row is standing upright through frames 19-25, then tilts and falls progressively rightward from frame 26 to frame 31.
The falling white row knocks the adjacent green domino at the junction around frames 31-32.

From frame 33 to 41 the collapse propagates from the junction into the colored chain: the leftmost red, yellow and green dominoes of the S-curve fall in sequence, moving up along the curve, while the rest of the colored loop and the right white row remain standing.
Camera position is static within each view; the apparent motion is object motion, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the initial fall in each white row is not shown; the segment begins with motion already underway in the first view.
What happens after frame 41 (whether the colored chain fully collapses) is not captured.
Whether the two views are part of the same physical run or separate setups is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact extent and speed of the falling wave in the right white row of the first view is hard to read against the static background.
The trajectory of the drifting green piece in the first view (slide vs. knock-away) cannot be determined from the frames alone.
Fine differences between consecutive frames in the second view reflect a smooth propagation; the precise frame of each domino's toppling is approximate.
